Documentation¶

The gss_export package exports the Prover iLock GSS as HLL.

The following files are produced:

  • SafetyProperties.hll: Contains the requirement definitions and the safety property proof obligations.
  • Deviations.hll: Contains requirement deviation definitions.
  • Sorts.hll: Defines the types used in quantifiers and functions.
  • DeclarationsINT.hll: Contains function declarations for functions to access variables of the object model.
  • DeclarationsPAR.hll: Contains function declarations for functions to access parameters of the object model.
  • Pre.hll: Contains auxilliary variables for making expressions using the PRE operator have a well-defined value in the first cycle.
  • Lemmas.hll: Contains auxilliary proof obligations to help the proof engine.

The exported HLL files do not make up a complete HLL system. In particular, it is up to the users of this package to provide definitions for the the functions declared in DeclararationsINT.hll and DeclarationsPAR.hll.

The content of gss_export is owned by Prover Technology AB.

Basic usage¶

import UtilityAPI

from gss_export.api import export_gss
from gss_export.config import Config, Reporter

def report_note(msg):
  UtilityAPI.LogNote(msg)

def report_warning(msg):
  UtilityAPI.LogWarning(msg)

def report_error(msg):
  UtilityAPI.LogError(msg)


reporter = Reporter(report_note, report_warning, report_error)
config = Config(
    out_dir="/path/to/out/dir",
    req_class_names=["SAFETY_PROGRAM"],
    reporter=reporter,
    generic_header="This is safety critical data. Do not modify.",
)
config.req_prefix = "GSS-"
res = export_gss(config)
if res.success:
  print("GSS data exported to /path/to/out/dir")

Restrictions on PiSPEC GSS¶

In order for translation to be successful, the PiSPEC GSS must adhere to a few rules.

  • Only safety properties starting with a specified prefix (default “GSS-”) will be exported. All other safety properties are interpreted as lemmas. This is because there is no distinction in PiSPEC between safety properties and lemmas.
  • Only types, functions, parameters and variables referred to (directly or indirectly) by such safety properties will be present in Sorts.hll, DeclarationsINT.hll, and DeclarationsPAR.hll.
  • Only PiSPEC functions that are not overriden (i.e. have a single implementation) may be used. Note that this applies transitively.
  • Functions with the same name, but different arity, in the same class may not be used. This is to preserve the PiSPEC name in HLL, without risking collisions.
  • A parameter can only be used if it has a single source. i.e. it can only be inherited from one place if multiple inheritance is used.
  • All variables, functions, safety properties, and equations across all GSS classes to be exported must have a unique name. This is because they will be merged into one single namespace, and we want to use the same names in PiSPEC and HLL.
  • For the moment, the PiSPEC COND operator is not supported.
  • Deviations may only refer to types and functions that are also referred to by the GSS. This is because deviations are SA (specific application) data, whereas the GSS itself is GA (generic application) data. The presence of deviations in a project should not affect the GA.

Using deviations¶

By default, no deviations are used. Set deviations_filename of the Config object if you want to use deviations.

Special variables¶

Variables marked with the PiSPEC attribute “SpecialVariable” are treated in a special way:

  • If the value of the attribute is “Init”, the variable will be mapped to an expression that is true in the first cycle, and false in subsequent cycles.
  • All other values of the attribute are ignored. In particular, the package does not support the values “StableState” and “FailureMode” at the moment.

Overview of translation¶

Each safety requirement is mapped to one HLL proof obligation, one HLL function defining the safety requirement itself, and one HLL function defining deviations for the safety requirement. We use the following PiSPEC to illustrate this translation process:

class SAFETY_PROGRAM {
Prove:
 "GSS-simple-req" := true;
 "GSS-univerally-quantified-req" :=
   ALL si: true;
}

For the PiSPEC above, the translator would output the following SafetyProperties.hll

Declarations:
  bool 'GSS-simple-req';
  bool 'GSS-universally-quantified-req'(SIGNAL);

Definitions:
  'GSS-simple-req' :=
    TRUE;

  'GSS-universally-quantified-req'(si) :=
    TRUE;

Declarations:
  bool 'PO_GSS-simple-req';
  bool 'PO_universally-quantified-req';

Definitions:
  'PO_GSS-simple-req' :=
    ~DEVIATIONS::'DEV_GSS-simple-req' ->
      'GSS-simple-req';

  'PO_GSS-simple-req' :=
    ALL si:SIGNAL (
      ~DEVIATIONS::'DEV_GSS-universally-quantified-req'(si) ->
        'GSS-universally-quantified-req'(si);

Proof obligations:
  'PO_GSS-simple-req';
  'PO_GSS-univerally-quantified-req';

As illustrated above, safety requirements starting with a universal quantifier are translated to functions taking a parameter of the type quantified over. This is so that the deviation and requirement can talk about the same instance.

“DEV_GSS-simple-req” and “DEV_GSS-universally-quantified” are defined in Deviations.hll, and default to FALSE if no deviation has been specified.
